The base face seats on three annular pads (dia 7.0 round each dia 3.0 x 0.5 pocket, trimmed 0.75 inside the plate outline), not on the whole face; the ball gauge plate of assembly step 2 carries the base plate on three bosses dia 7.0 round its gauge holes, its face 0.3 lower elsewhere; every depth reading on the underside (ring crest, potting level, rim relief) is taken with a bridge gauge on three annular feet dia 6.0 / 1.6 round the balls. deviations.reason: a printed legend stands about 0.02 mm proud of the mask (0.03 at most) and the tub rim is only 0.25 above the base plane. On a full-face hard seat the marker would rest on ink islands, on a bowed plate or on the rim (0.02 mm across the foot triangle is about 0.8 mrad); on a flat gauge plate the ink would add itself to the ball protrusion (0.1 +-0.02) and take the same 0.03 from the epoxy between ball and land (0.02 at the lower plate limit); a depth gauge resting on legend 1.2 mm from the grain opening would read the potting level that much deep against a never-below limit of 0.05. Three points next to the feet on bare mask are one reference plane for all of these, and they measure what E11 is about: the plane of the base face against the plane of the balls. A laser-marked legend has no height and would not need this

deviations.requirement: quarter-wave film, about 0.1 mm, on the underside of the cover glass, axis 45 deg to the LCD polariser; 1.08 mm of air between display and glass, so nothing else moves (E9)

Outside the dia 22.0 aperture it lies over the roof ledge in the 0.13 mm gap that the tape leaves: 0.03 mm nominal, 0.007 mm with the tape at its thinnest and the film 0.01 thicker
deviations.reason: the air gap of 1.08 mm exists only inside the aperture.
